correctness.rationale: The crown graph is (n-1)-regular, giving the exact threshold t=floor((n-1)/2) for selected neighbors. For occupied shore index sets X,Y, chosen a_i has |Y|-1_{i in Y} selected neighbors and chosen b_j has |X|-1_{j in X}. These counts prove the complete alliance feasibility dichotomy (both shores >=t+1, or both >=t and disjoint). Single-deletion analysis leaves exactly disjoint (t,t) and intersecting (t+1,t+1) with overlap >=2. For the latter, any proper alliance must delete one selected vertex on each shore, removing all overlap, which is possible if and only if overlap=2; with overlap>=3 global minimality follows. Binomial choices yield all labelled polynomial coefficients. Boundaries n=3,4 have t=1 and no overlap>=3. The standalone script independently checked original neighborhood inequalities, all locally/globally minimal sets, and closed counts through n=8 (87,360 labelled subsets). The unrestricted conclusion relies on the proof, not the finite check.

originality.rationale: Compared the actual characterization, overlap thresholds, full labelled coefficients and upper-parameter implications with accessible foundational, parameterized and enumeration literature and accessible earlier scientific results. Bazgan–Fernau–Tuza introduce the local/global distinction and general upper problems but no crown classification in inspected material. Gaikwad–Maity give FPT and hardness results rather than the closed intersection theorem. Searches did not find an equivalent exact crown formula. Feng–Fernau–Mann (2023) and Fernau et al. (2026) are highly relevant generic enumeration papers whose primary full texts could not be read, creating a material publication-priority residual risk; this risk does not establish coverage but warrants independent comparison. Small n=3 is a six-cycle, and no new priority is asserted for its isolated specialization.

value.rationale: Globally versus locally minimal defensive alliances differ because the property is nonhereditary, and upper/all-cardinality distinctions are explicitly motivated in the source literature. On an infinite, connected, regular bipartite family the exact overlap-two local-only obstruction is a structural classification: each such set contains exactly two strictly smaller globally minimal alliances. Both full labelled polynomials, possible minimal cardinalities and both upper parameters follow, with a sharp n=5 boundary for agreement of upper values despite persistent family-level disagreement. Neither a scalar minimum nor the ability to enumerate algorithmically supplies this statement.
